vendors.name: Knostic Kirin
vendors.offering: In-agent policy checks on every coding-agent tool call, MCP validation across Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot
vendors.pricing: Free for 1-5 users; Team $15/user/month; Enterprise via sales

vendors.name: Pillar Security (Pillar for AI Coding Agents)
vendors.offering: Discovers local coding agents, scans permissions/MCP configs, runtime detection of prompt injection and tool abuse
vendors.pricing: AWS Marketplace: Pillar Security Platform $175,000/12 months

vendors.name: Lasso Security
vendors.offering: Inspects coding-agent and MCP tool calls and scans tool outputs before the agent acts
vendors.pricing: code-assistant price not public; AWS Marketplace annual commits $20,000 (GenAI Chatbots) and $50,000 (LLM gateway) per 12 months

vendors.name: Prompt Security (SentinelOne)
vendors.offering: MCP gateway with allow/block/redact per call; covers AI code assistants like Cursor

vendors.name: Runlayer
vendors.offering: MCP control layer watching every agent action, blocking suspicious calls, audit logs

vendors.name: Invariant Labs Guardrails
vendors.offering: MCP/LLM proxy gateway enforcing deterministic contextual rules and tool-call restrictions

vendors.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy
vendors.offering: Cedar policies check every agent tool call through AgentCore Gateway, allow or deny
vendors.pricing: usage-based, per authorization request (rate not captured) plus per-token natural-language authoring

vendors.name: Docker MCP Gateway
vendors.offering: Open-source MCP proxy running servers in restricted containers with access control and call tracing
vendors.pricing: gateway open source; Docker AI Governance version invite-only, price not public

paid_market_gaps.gap: Enterprise platforms sell via large annual commits (Pillar $175k, Lasso $20k+); small teams have few paid options besides Knostic.
Native agent permission rules are pattern-based; argument rules are bypassable by compound commands, pushing users to sandboxing.
Headless/non-interactive agent runs often auto-approve all tool calls, with no read-only or plan mode.
Per-call policy engines do not yet correlate sequences of individually allowed calls into malicious workflows.

wtp_evidence: Public prices exist: Pillar platform $175,000/12 months and Lasso for GenAI Chatbots $20,000 annual commit (12 months) on AWS Marketplace, Knostic Kirin $15/user/month.
bundling_note: Agent vendors ship free permission rules and managed deny settings (Claude Code), AWS meters Cedar tool-call policy in AgentCore, and Microsoft and Docker give away open-source MCP policy gateways.
summary: Crowded and consolidating (SentinelOne-Prompt, well-funded Pillar, Lasso, Runlayer) with free native and cloud controls. Narrow opening: cheap cross-agent policy enforcement for small and mid-size dev teams, including headless/CI agent runs, below enterprise annual commits.
